# Enter-to-end-turn browser wait exceeds the 60 s hook above ~2x CPU oversubscription

## Headline

The `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` wait in
`tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` is already at the largest
budget the 60 s browser hook permits (40 000 ms = 16 000 ms cap + 24 000 ms
margin + 20 000 ms boot = 60 000 ms), yet it fails at ≈2× CPU oversubscription
because the bounded end-of-turn deferral is re-polled on Phaser's clamped game
clock, so the forced day start is detected late. **Decision: make the
deferral's safety cap starvation-proof** — one extracted helper whose deadline
and re-poll run on wall clock, enforced even while the page is not painting
(producer, Q1 = C, Q2 = 1).

## Problem statement

The soak evidence on MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L shows the gate passes 20/20 quiet
(peak load 15.3), passes 2/2 at 8 burners (peak 23.6), and fails exactly one
wait — `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` — at load ≥ ≈31
(≈2× oversubscription, 16 burners, peak 32.8). That wait's budget is already at
the ceiling the 60 s hook permits, so no poll-budget tweak inside the hook can
rescue it.

Root cause (mechanism, verified against the installed `phaser` source):
Phaser's `TimeStep` clamps the per-frame delta it feeds scenes — under
`smoothStep` (default on) each frame contributes at most `1000/fps.min`
(200 ms) — and `Clock.elapsed`, which drives `delayedCall` timers and tween
progress, advances by that clamped delta. Under starvation (a few frames per
second) all game-time-paced choreography stretches: income phase gaps, coin
flights, the incident hold, and the deferral's own 250 ms `delayedCall`
re-polls. The deferral *deadline* (`s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`,
where `s.time.now` is the raw frame timestamp) is wall-clock, but it is only
re-checked at those clamped polls, so the forced day start is delayed by the
same starvation. Aggregate: closing choreography (stretched) + 16 s cap
(late-detected) + boot > the 40 s budget and the 60 s hook.

The cap's stated purpose is "end-of-turn can never hang the game"
(CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q, AC5/AC7). A stall bound that is only observed at frame
boundaries does not provide that guarantee — which is what this item fixes,
without touching the user-visible pacing.

## Users

- **Agent-implementer / gate runner** on the shared dev host: needs the browser
  gate green; a red `MainStreetScene` suite at ≈2× oversubscription burns whole
  sessions on retries and blocks the build → test → commit order.
- **Maintainer triaging a red browser suite**: needs a red wait to mean a
  behavioural regression, not host weather.
- **Release engineer** on the dev-push gate: a red gate on a loaded shared host
  stalls shipping even when the scene is correct.
- **Players**: unchanged pacing — the choreography, the incident hold and the
  cap value all stay as shipped; only the cap's *enforcement* becomes
  wall-clock rather than frame-clock, so under starvation the day advances at
  the documented bound instead of stalling past it.

Example user stories:

> As an agent running the browser gate on the shared 16-core host, I want the
> Enter-to-end-turn wait to pass at any load the host actually reaches, so that
> my gate result does not depend on which sibling suites happen to be running.

> As a player whose machine is momentarily overloaded, I want the end-of-turn
> to still advance within the documented safety window, so that the game can
> never appear hung.

## Existing state

- Measured envelope (2026-10-24, 16-core shared host): quiet 20/20 pass
  (peak 15.3); 8 burners 2/2 pass, then one fail at ambient 31.3; 16 burners
  fail at the 40 000 ms end-of-turn budget. Every other wait in the file passes
  at that load.
- The wait's effective budget is `capMs: INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` (16 000) +
  `floorMs: END_TURN_STARVATION_MARGIN_MS` (24 000) = 40 000 ms, the largest
  that keeps the documented 20 000 ms scene-boot allowance inside the 60 s
  `testTimeout` (asserted by `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts`). The
  suite's per-test timeout is already `it(..., 60_000)`.
- Five deferral polls race the choreography, all with the same shape
  (`startAt = <scene clock> + cap`, then `delayedCall(250, poll)`):
  3 in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` (`advanceTurn` ~433,
  forced event-choice ~617, piggyback ~783) and 2 in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` (`finish`'s income wait
  ~254 and the reveal gating ~301).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` already has the
  degradation precedent: `scheduleOrRun` runs the callback immediately when the
  scene has no clock (headless), which a wall-clock helper must preserve.
- Node unit suites drive these polls through fake `time` stubs
  (`tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts`), and
  `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` pins "exactly three
  `s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` sites" by regex — both must be
  updated by the extraction.
- Reduced motion clears `incomeCollectionActive` synchronously in
  `MainStreetAnimatorIncome` (~line 1039), but it is **not** the remedy chosen:
  the parent rejected it as the sole remedy because it removes the
  deferred-income path from coverage.

## Desired change (decision: option C)

Replace the five duplicated deferral polls with **one shared, injectable
helper** that:

1. computes its deadline from a wall-clock timestamp (`Date.now()`),
2. re-polls with a wall-clock timer (`window.setTimeout`), not the scene clock,
3. forces completion (clearing `incomeCollectionActive` and invoking the
   caller's continuation) once `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` of wall time has
   elapsed since the deferral began,
4. is enforced even when the page is not painting — a backgrounded/hidden
   document ahead of the cap forces the advance rather than waiting for the
   next animation frame (Q2 = 1), and
5. degrades to today's behaviour where no clock/timer exists (headless node
   scenes run the continuation immediately), and exposes its clock/timer for
   deterministic unit driving.

Options considered and rejected (recorded for traceability):

- **A — accept and document the envelope** (no code change): the gate can still
  go red on the shared host when ambient load spikes ≥2×, conflicting with the
  "red tree never pushed" policy; rejected in favour of a root-cause fix.
- **B — reduced-motion Enter test + a separate cheap deferral-contract test**:
  no production change, but downgrades the file's end-to-end end-of-turn test
  to a synthetic and couples coverage to a reduced-motion implementation
  detail; retained only as a fallback if C's soak does not pass.
- **D — raise the browser hook for this test**: pure masking, requires
  amending the parent's "any derived budget must leave headroom for boot plus
  teardown within that hook" AC and re-baselining the guard's headroom rule,
  and would fail again at ≈4× oversubscription; rejected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **One bounded-deferral helper, wall-clock enforced.** All five
      income-collection deferral polls route through a single shared helper
      whose deadline is wall clock and whose re-poll is a wall timer; no inline
      `s.time.delayedCall(250, <poll>)` / `<scene clock> + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`
      poll remains. A unit test with a frozen scene clock and an advancing wall
      clock proves the continuation is forced within one poll interval of the
      16 000 ms cap.
- [ ] **Forced advance is not tied to paint.** When the document is hidden / no
      frame runs, the cap still forces the advance after the cap elapses
      (Q2 = 1). A unit test asserts the wall timer — not the scene clock —
      drives the assertion, and the behaviour is documented in the module's
      code comment.
- [ ] **Injectable and backward-compatible.** The helper accepts an injectable
      clock/timer (so `competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
      `turnflow.test.ts` and the new tests drive it deterministically) and
      preserves today's no-clock degradation (headless scenes run the
      continuation immediately).
- [ ] **Single source of truth for the cap.** `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` stays
      16 000 and remains the only cap value; the
      `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` "exactly three
      `s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` sites" pin is updated to the
      helper extraction (asserting the helper consumes the constant), so the
      duplication cannot silently return.
- [ ] **No production pacing change.** The choreography timing constants
      (`INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS`, flight/stagger durations, `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS`)
      and the cap value are unchanged — pinned by existing/added unit tests;
      only the cap's enforcement mechanism differs.
- [ ] **Wait-budget guard still green.** `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts`
      passes unchanged: the end-of-turn wait keeps its cap-derived 40 000 ms
      budget and `budget + 20 s boot ≤ 60 s` headroom rule. If the soak shows
      the budget can now be reduced, that reduction is a *derived* margin
      change proved by the soak, not a hand-picked literal.
- [ ] **Reliability proven, not assumed.** `/skill:test --type soak-load`
      (≥ `nproc` burners) passes with the change, and the pre-change failure at
      the same burner count is reproduced and recorded on this item; both
      before/after tables (burners, peak load, runs, wall times, summary paths)
      are posted as a comment.
- [ ] **Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/testing.md` "Measured envelope" and
      the headroom rule section record the decision (cap enforced on wall
      clock, hidden-tab semantics) and the post-fix envelope, replacing the
      "above ~2× is outside the envelope" caveat with measured evidence; the
      helper's module comment documents the wall-clock contract. All related
      documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
      README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes
      (`/skill:test --type full`), evidence recorded on this item.

## Constraints

- **No behavioural change to production pacing.** The choreography, the
  incident hold and the cap value are shipped features
  (CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ, CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q); only the cap's enforcement may
  change.
- The parent's headroom constraint stands: `budget + scene-boot allowance` must
  stay inside the browser 60 s hook.
- Reduced motion must not become the sole remedy (parent decision); the
  deferred-income path keeps explicit coverage.
- All five deferral sites must keep identical semantics after extraction, and
  the existing fake-clock unit suites must not be weakened to accommodate the
  change.
- A stale wall timer must never fire into a destroyed scene — reuse the
  existing `scene.isActive()` / try-catch defensive pattern from the deferred
  closing tail.
- Agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill only
  (`/skill:test --type soak-load`, `--type full`); no ad-hoc `npx vitest` loops.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` — add the shared
  wall-clock deferral helper (sibling to `scheduleOrRun` ~line 176); adopt it in
  `finish`'s income wait (~254) and the reveal gating (~301).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — three deferral sites
  (`advanceTurn` ~433, forced event-choice ~617, piggyback ~783) adopt the
  helper.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` — `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`
  unchanged; comment updated to state the wall-clock enforcement contract.
- `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` — the "exactly three
  `s.time.now + cap` sites" regex pin moves to the helper extraction.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts` — fake `time` stubs: drive the injected
  timer/clock.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` — Enter test and its
  40 000 ms margin expected unchanged.
- `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts` — headroom rule re-check (expected
  unchanged).
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — "Measured envelope" + headroom rule: record the
  decision and the post-fix soak evidence.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the clamped-delta mechanism is the dominant starvation link
  and the deferral's poll cadence is the part that can be fixed without touching
  pacing. Verified against the installed Phaser source
  (`TimeStep.smoothDelta`, `Clock.now` / `Clock.elapsed` semantics); the
  before/after `soak-load` run is the confirmation.
- **Risk:** removing the late-detection link may not be sufficient on its own —
  the choreography phases before/after the deferral still stretch under
  clamped delta. Mitigation: the soak is a hard AC; if it still fails, the
  fallback is option B's separate deferral-contract test (not option D), and
  the residual envelope is re-documented with evidence.
- **Risk (accepted, decided):** a wall-clock cap changes hidden/backgrounded-tab
  behaviour — the day start is now forced after the cap instead of stalling
  until the tab paints again (Q2 = 1). This is the intended semantics of a stall
  bound; documented in the module comment and `docs/dev/testing.md`.
- **Risk:** a wall timer outliving the scene could fire into a destroyed scene.
  Mitigation: `scene.isActive()` guard plus the existing try-catch pattern; a
  unit test covers the destroyed/stale case.
- **Risk (scope creep):** the attractor is "rework all game-time animation off
  clamped delta" (tweens, phase gaps, incident hold). Explicitly out of scope —
  record as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Related work

- MS-0MVMKEU2000639TG — this item (`discovered-from:` the soak child
  MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L; soak evidence and envelope recorded there and in
  `docs/dev/testing.md` "Measured envelope").
- MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — parent: made the file's waits load-tolerant via
  cap-derived budgets; its headroom AC and "Measured limit (triaged, not a
  flake)" section are the origin of this item.
- MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L — the 20-run / under-load soak whose evidence defines the
  envelope and whose `soak-load` profile proves this fix.
- MS-0MVLINWV10005H2P — the wait-budget guard and headroom rule this item must
  keep green.
- MS-0MUYFX7Q2004JQ5R — shared end-of-turn closing presentation primitive that
  carries `incomeCollectionCapMs`.
- CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ / CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q — phased income choreography and
  deferred income window (untouched pacing; the property the cap protects).
- MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 (open) — planned End-of-Turn summary dialog on the
  closing completion path; it will interact with the deferral this item
  extracts, so check dependency direction during planning.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L** – Prove browser-wait reliability: 20-run soak plus under-load run (completed)
- **MS-0MVLINWV10005H2P** – Guard browser wait budgets against production caps (completed)
- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** – End of Turn summary… (open; planned dialog on the closing path)

### Related repository files
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — engine developer guide; frame-loop/delta context.
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — measured envelope and headroom rule this item updates.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — documents reduced motion, deferral pacing and
  presentation behaviour these waits must respect.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Given the measured envelope (the gate fails only above ≈2× CPU
  oversubscription, load ≥ ~31), which remediation should this item
  implement — (A) accept and document the envelope with no code change,
  (B) convert the Enter test to reduced motion plus a separate cheap
  deferral-contract test, (C) make the income-collection deferral cap
  starvation-proof (wall-clock deadline + wall-clock poll, one extracted
  helper, production change confined to the safety cap), or (D) raise the
  browser hook for this test (parent AC amendment needed)?"
  — Answer (producer): **C** — make the income-collection deferral cap
  starvation-proof. Source: interactive reply (intake interview round 1,
  2026-10-25). Agent recommendation was C (stated with rationale before the
  answer); A was recorded as the zero-production-change fallback and B's second
  variant as the fallback if C's soak still fails. Research behind the
  recommendation: Phaser `TimeStep.smoothDelta` clamps per-frame delta to
  `1000/fps.min` (200 ms default), so under rAF starvation the choreography and
  the deferral's 250 ms `delayedCall` re-polls both run at a fraction of
  wall-clock speed — the wall-clock cap deadline is therefore detected late,
  which is the link C removes.
- Q2 (conditional on C): "Should the 16 000 ms cap be enforced against wall
  clock even when the page is not painting/visible (backgrounded tab or fully
  starved rAF — the day start is forced after 16 s wall even though the
  choreography never ran), or should the forced advance hold while the document
  is hidden/blurred and resume on visibility change?"
  — Answer (producer): **as recommended** = enforce on wall clock (option 1):
  the cap is a stall bound, nothing is visible while hidden, and today a hidden
  tab already stalls the animator indefinitely. Source: interactive reply
  (intake interview round 1, 2026-10-25). Recorded as an accepted, documented
  semantic change in the Risks section and to be reflected in the helper's
  module comment and `docs/dev/testing.md`.
data.title: Enter-to-end-turn browser wait exceeds the 60 s hook above ~2x CPU oversubscription

# Bankruptcy bailout offer, AI policy and headless resolution

Parent: MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (Bank Loans). Depends on the takeLoan command and repayment
slices.

## Goal

When a seat would go bankrupt with no active loan, the run does not end: the seat is
offered a loan instead, may accept (principal credited, play continues) or decline
(today's bankruptcy), while an AI seat auto-accepts the largest option and headless runs
never stall.

## Context

- Bankruptcy is currently terminal in two places in `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`:
  `checkImmediateLoss` (single-player, `coins < 0` → `endReason 'bankruptcy'`) and
  `resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures` (competitive seats). This slice handles the
  **single-player** path; competitive parity is the next slice.
- The established pending-decision pattern is `state.pendingEventChoice` /
  `state.pendingPiggyback`: the closing pauses (returns `choicePending` /
  `piggybackPending` with `requiresDeferredClosing`), the UI resolves the decision, then the
  closing tail re-runs. `state.pendingLoanOffer` must follow the same shape, with a
  `pendingLoanOffer` flag on `TurnResult`.
- Ordering matters: the bailout intercept must run **before** `checkImmediateLoss` /
  `checkEndConditions`, and must respect `applyFirstSharedDaySolvencyGrace`
  (MS-0MVJNFESC005QJ41 — no player is bankrupt on the opening day).
- Producer decisions: Q3=A (bailout only, no proactive AI lending), Q5=A (AI auto-accepts
  the **largest** option), Q6=A (shortfall unconditional). At most one offer per seat per
  turn — a decline must converge to game over in a single pass, never loop.
- Headless: `endTurnHeadless` (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`) and the Monte Carlo
  runner must resolve a pending offer deterministically with the AI policy; they must never
  leave a pending pause open.

## Desired change

1. `maybeOfferBailout(state)` in `src/MainStreetLoans.ts`: when the acting seat is at
   `coins < 0`, holds no active loan, loans are enabled and no offer has already been made
   this turn, set `pendingLoanOffer = { ownerId, reason: 'bankruptcy', options }` and return
   "pause" so the closing defers instead of declaring the loss.
2. `acceptLoanOffer(state, option)` / `declineLoanOffer(state)` resolve the pending offer
   (accept runs the `takeLoan` path, decline clears the offer and lets the loss declaration
   stand), then the caller re-runs/completes the closing tail exactly once.
3. `TurnResult` gains `pendingLoanOffer` (mirroring `choicePending` / `piggybackPending`),
   and the per-turn "already offered" guard so a second evaluation in the same turn cannot
   re-offer.
4. AI/headless: auto-accept the largest option (deterministic tie-break: largest principal,
   then longest term) in the AI and headless paths; no proactive loans anywhere.
5. Tests: offer on bankruptcy with no loan, accept credits principal and play continues,
   decline → bankruptcy, second offer in the same turn suppressed, AI largest-option
   auto-accept and AI survival (not eliminated), shortfall with an active loan → bankruptcy
   without an offer, headless determinism (no stalled pending offer), first-turn grace
   respected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a seat would fail on coins < 0 in single-player play and holds no active loan, the game does not end: a loan offer is presented instead, accepting credits the principal and play continues, while declining preserves today's bankruptcy behaviour.
- At most one bailout offer is made per seat per turn (no offer loop), and a seat that already holds an active loan preserves today's bankruptcy behaviour.
- An AI seat that hits coins < 0 with no active loan auto-accepts the largest loan option and is not eliminated, and AI seats take no proactive (non-bailout) loans.
- Headless turn execution never stalls on a pending loan offer and resolves deterministically using the AI bailout policy.
- Unit tests cover bailout offer/accept/decline, shortfall → bankruptcy and the AI largest-option policy.

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — `maybeOfferBailout`, `acceptLoanOffer`, `declineLoanOffer`
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — intercept before `checkImmediateLoss`, deferred-closing pause/resume
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — `pendingLoanOffer` on `TurnResult`
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — AI bailout auto-accept (largest option)
- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — headless resolution of a pending offer
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanBailout.test.ts` — new bailout/AI/headless tests
data.title: Bailout offer, AI policy and headless resolution

# Bailout overlay UI and deferred closing resume

Parent: MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (Bank Loans). Depends on the single-player bailout slice.

## Goal

When a bailout offer is open, the player sees a dialog listing the loan options with their
per-turn and total repayment plus a Decline button, and accepting or declining resumes the
turn exactly once.

## Context

- Overlay conventions: `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` from `@ui`, all
  elements parented into `s.hudContainer`, depths 199/200/201, every object pushed into
  `s.overlayObjects`, `safePlaySound` for SFX, reduced-motion safe instant appearance.
- Precedents: `showEventChoiceDialog` / `showPiggybackDialog` /
  `showTurnSummaryDialog` in `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`, delegated from
  `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts`; pure Phaser-free models such as
  `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` (`MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` is the newest
  example) keep the content testable without a browser.
- Resume path: the deferred closing tail is re-run from
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` (`finishTurnPresentation` /
  `finishDeferredTurnClosing`) — the same shape used for pending event choices.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` must not present game-over while a bailout
  offer is open, but must present the normal bankruptcy summary after a decline.
- The Turn Summary "Bank Loan" button (`onBankLoanAction` seam in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` / `MainStreetScene.ts`) is deliberately a
  separate follow-up item — do not wire it here.

## Desired change

1. New pure model `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlayModel.ts` (or equivalent) building the
   option rows from `pendingLoanOffer` + `config.loanOptions`: principal, per-turn
   repayment, total repayment, term.
2. New `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` rendering the dialog with one button per
   option and a Decline button, following the overlay conventions above.
3. Wire presentation into the turn controller: when `result.pendingLoanOffer` is set, show
   the overlay instead of the game-over summary; on resolution call the loan accept/decline
   handler and then run the deferred closing tail exactly once.
4. Tests: model test for the option rows, overlay browser test for render + button count +
   dismiss behaviour, and a turn-flow test proving the closing resumes once (no replay, no
   duplicate offer).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A bailout overlay is rendered whenever a pending loan offer exists, listing each loan option with its per-turn and total repayment plus a Decline choice.
- Accepting or declining the offer resumes the deferred closing sequence, and the game-over summary is not shown while a bailout offer is open.
- Tests assert the overlay is presented once per offer, the resume completes the closing exactly once, and no replay or duplicate-offer loop occurs.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` — new overlay dialog
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — dialog presentation following the event-choice pattern
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — delegation method
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — deferred-closing resume wiring
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — suppress game-over while an offer is open
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanOverlay.test.ts` — new model/flow tests
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanOverlay.browser.test.ts` — new overlay browser test

# Persistence: loans and pending offer, save schema v3

Parent: MS-0MVL6DZI0000F6CG (Bank Loans). Depends on the loan model and bailout slices.

## Goal

A save taken mid-loan (or mid-offer) restores exactly: active loans keep their remaining
turns and repayment amounts, a pending bailout offer is still pending, and pre-loan saves
load unchanged.

## Context

- `serializeMainStreetState` / `deserializeMainStreetState`
  (`src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`) with `MAIN_STREET_SAVE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2` and a
  strict version check plus `migrateSerializedState` hook (`src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts`).
  Bumping to 3 with defaults is the established path for new fields.
- The migration must default legacy saves to an empty `loans` list and no pending offer, so
  a pre-loan save continues with unchanged behaviour (parent AC9).
- Existing coverage: `tests/main-street/save-load.test.ts` and
  `tests/main-street/CalendarSaveLoad.test.ts` show the round-trip/migration test shape;
  the migration browser test (`tests/main-street/MainStreetMigration.browser.test.ts`)
  covers legacy browser saves.
- Campaign save data (`MAIN_STREET_CAMPAIGN_SCHEMA_VERSION`) is separate — do not bump it
  unless a field genuinely needs it.

## Desired change

1. Serialise `loans` (all fields needed to resume the schedule: principal, total,
   per-turn, turns remaining, term, ownerId) and `pendingLoanOffer` (owner, reason,
   options); omit or null them when empty so diffs stay small.
2. Bump `MAIN_STREET_SAVE_SCHEMA_VERSION` to 3, add a v2 → v3 migration defaulting to no
   loans and no pending offer, and accept v2 saves through it.
3. Restore defensively: unknown/invalid loan entries are dropped rather than crashing the
   load, and `turnsRemaining` is clamped to `termTurns`.
4. Tests: round-trip with an active loan (remaining turns and per-turn amount preserved),
   round-trip with a pending offer, v2 save loads with empty loans and unchanged behaviour,
   and a mid-loan save resumes with the correct remaining payments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Active loans and a pending loan offer survive a save/load round-trip, and the save schema version is bumped to 3 with a migration.
- Pre-loan saves at schema version 2 load with no loans and unchanged behaviour, proven by a migration test.

# Phaser 4 + WebGL: `GeometryMask` `setMask` is a no-op, so the street map and log viewports are unclipped

Discovered-from: MS-0MVRDVVH4001048Q (reputation crowd regression diagnosis, MS-0MVRMHS4S0067RRQ).

## Problem

The game runs Phaser `4.0.0-rc.7`. In Phaser 4 the WebGL renderer no longer supports `GameObject.setMask` with a `GeometryMask`; it logs and returns immediately:

```js
// node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/components/Mask.js
setMask: function (mask) {
    if (this.scene.renderer.type === CONST.WEBGL) {
        console.warn('Phaser.GameObjects.Components.Mask.setMask: This method is not supported in WebGL. Create a Mask filter instead.');
        return this;
    }
```

Observed on every street refresh of the real scene (WebGL, normal play):

```
Phaser.GameObjects.Components.Mask.setMask: This method is not supported in WebGL. Create a Mask filter instead.
```

Call sites in this repo that therefore do nothing under WebGL:

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts:611` — `s.streetContainer.setMask(mask)` (the street map viewport mask, `installStreetMapMask` / `updateStreetMapMask`)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts:331` — `s.logContentContainer.setMask(s.logContentMask)` (Activity Log scroll clipping)
- core: `core/src/ui/HelpPanel.ts:524`, `core/src/ui/Overlay.ts:484`, `core/src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts:909` (core-owned; raise/route in core rather than editing the submodule)

Consequences in a WebGL boot: the street map is no longer clipped to the street viewport (it can draw over neighbouring panels/outside its band) and the Activity Log content is no longer clipped to its scroll area. The Canvas path (used by most browser tests) still honours the masks, so the regression is invisible to the test suite.

### Which renderer actually boots (verified 2026-10-29, plan)

The defect is **latent in the shipped launcher build and live in any WebGL boot**:

- `index.html` loads `/main.ts` (the scaffolded launcher entry), which calls `createCardGame({ …, type: Phaser.CANVAS })` — the packaged game is Canvas, so the masks still work there.
- `src/main.ts` (the standalone game entry) calls `createMainStreetGameWithPacks()` → `createCardGame` whose default is `type: renderType ?? Phaser.AUTO` (`core/src/ui/createCardGame.ts:123`) — that is WebGL on any GPU-capable browser.
- `tests/main-street/hud-total-counting-live.browser.test.ts:46` boots `createMainStreetGame()` with **no** `type`, i.e. AUTO → WebGL, so the warning path is already reachable from the test suite.

So this is a real defect that blocks/degrades the WebGL renderer (`MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK`), not a cosmetic log line. See the OPEN QUESTIONs in the Appendix about prioritisation and scope.

## Notes / scope

- Not the cause of the crowd regression: an unclipped container renders *more*, not less, and the crowd was verified present, attached, textured and on-screen under WebGL (see `tests/main-street/pedestrians-scene-visibility.browser.test.ts`).
- Fix direction: Phaser 4 mask **filters** (`FilterList.addMask` / `Phaser.Filters.Mask`) for the WebGL path, or a renderer-agnostic clipping approach; verify visually in the real WebGL build and keep the Canvas behaviour unchanged.
- **Risky assumption (unproven in rc.7):** `addMask` lives on `Phaser.GameObjects.Components.FilterList`, which `Container` does *not* mix in (`node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/container/Container.js` mixes in `Mask`, `Transform`, `Visible`, … but not `FilterList`); `Container` does inherit the `Filters` component from `GameObject`. Applying a Mask filter to a `Container` (or `streetContainer` / `logContentContainer` specifically) is therefore **unverified**. Fallbacks, in preference order, if the filter path does not work: per-camera viewport clipping (a dedicated camera whose viewport is the street band / log content rect), restructuring the clipped content into a filtered `Layer`, or an explicit scissor/`setCrop`-style renderer hook. Confirm the approach before committing to a large refactor.
- **Partial mitigation already present:** `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts:814-830` hides log children whose local Y falls outside the visible window as a "safety net" for the unreliable GeometryMask clip. That hides fully-outside entries but cannot clip a partially-visible entry, so AC2 still stands.
- Canvas behaviour must not change: the GeometryMask path is correct under Canvas and is what the current test suite exercises. Prefer a renderer-branch (`scene.renderer.type === Phaser.WEBGL`) over a wholesale replacement so Canvas output stays byte-stable.
- Not in scope: the GPU card shader (`MS-0MUWNTQ5L0075Y38`) and the renderer switch itself.

### Related work (partial overlap — split of responsibilities)

- `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` — "Migrate Main Street renderer from Canvas to WebGL" (open, `plan_complete`, priority low). Its AC2 covers the *whole* GeometryMask → Mask-filter migration (core UI, gym scenes, Main Street) and its AC3 covers *creating* a WebGL browser-test project; both overlap this item. **Scope split:** this item owns the in-repo viewport-clipping defect (street map + Activity Log) and the console-warning regression assertion; `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` owns the launcher/core boot switch, the core-owned call sites, and the general WebGL test-project plumbing. The pattern established here is the reference implementation for that item's AC2.
- `MS-0MVRDVVH4001048Q` / `MS-0MVRMHTW6006KQKI` — the crowd regression this was discovered from (diagnosis complete; guard landed).
- `MS-0MV14JDUG000E1V6` — Activity Log rendering (completed); relevant to the log-viewport clip.
- Duplicate check performed (`wl search "mask webgl"`, `"GeometryMask clipping"`) — no completed item already satisfies these ACs; overlap with `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` is partial only (see above).

## Acceptance criteria

1. The street map viewport is clipped to `streetViewportRect` in the real WebGL renderer (no rendering outside the band; map scroll/zoom still clipped as before).
2. The Activity Log content is clipped to its scroll area under WebGL.
3. No `setMask … not supported in WebGL` console warning remains in a real-scene WebGL boot (assert in a browser test on the real renderer).
4. Canvas rendering behaviour and the existing layout/panel tests stay green; the full suite passes.
5. Core-owned call sites are fixed upstream (core work item) or explicitly documented as deferred.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — street map mask (`installStreetMapMask`/`updateStreetMapMask`, ~line 611) and log mask (~line 331) call sites
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — `logContentMask` / `streetMapMaskGraphics` field declarations (~line 257)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — log-scroll safety net (~line 814) that interacts with the log clip; also the `updateLogMask` caller
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` / `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererContext.ts` — mask install/update wiring
- `src/gym/GymCardIndexScene.ts` — third in-repo `setMask` site (`applyScroll`, ~line 373; `clearMask` ~line 683) — same bug class, see OPEN QUESTION 3
- `tests/main-street/pedestrians-scene-visibility.browser.test.ts` — real-scene boot harness to model the new WebGL test on (note: it boots `Phaser.CANVAS`, it is **not** an existing WebGL harness)
- `tests/main-street/hud-total-counting-live.browser.test.ts` — the only existing test that boots the real scene without a `type`, i.e. AUTO → WebGL; the natural place (or template) for the console-warning assertion in AC3
- `vite.config.ts` — `browser` project configuration (shared headless-Chromium context) if a WebGL boot needs launch args
- `src/README.md` — the "Viewport clipping" bullet (~line 105) currently states the street layer *is* clipped by a `GeometryMask`; must describe the renderer-dependent behaviour
- `docs/dev/testing.md` — browser-project conventions; note how to boot a WebGL browser test
- `docs/dev/` — no dedicated renderer doc exists today; add the Phaser 4 WebGL mask restriction note here (or in `src/README.md`) so the next reader does not repeat the diagnosis

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Recorded during the plan session (2026-10-29). Facts verified directly against the checkout rather than asked of the producer; producer decisions needed are labelled OPEN QUESTION.

- Q: Is the reported defect reproducible in the shipped build? — Answer (code, verified): partly. The launcher entry (`index.html` → `main.ts`) boots `Phaser.CANVAS`, so the packaged game is unaffected; `src/main.ts` and any `createMainStreetGame()` call without a `type` boot AUTO → WebGL, where `setMask` is a no-op. Evidence: `main.ts:23`, `src/main.ts:16`, `core/src/ui/createCardGame.ts:123`, `tests/main-street/hud-total-counting-live.browser.test.ts:46`.
- Q: Does an existing WebGL browser-test harness exist to extend for AC3? — Answer (code, verified): no. Every `*.browser.test.ts` that passes a renderer passes `Phaser.CANVAS` (77 call sites); `hud-total-counting-live.browser.test.ts` is the sole AUTO boot. AC3 therefore needs a new (or newly-WebGL-ified) browser test, not just an added assertion in an existing WebGL harness.
- Q: Is there already a planned item covering the GeometryMask migration? — Answer (code/wl, verified): yes, partially — `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` AC2/AC3. Scope split recorded under "Related work".
- **OPEN QUESTION 1 (producer, priority/urgency):** the packaged launcher is Canvas today, so the visible impact only lands when the WebGL migration ships (or via `src/main.ts`/AUTO boots). Should this item stay `medium` and be sequenced *before* `MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK` (recommended — it is that item's prerequisite pattern), or be raised to `high` because a WebGL boot is already reachable through `src/main.ts` and one browser test? Matters because it decides whether the migration item is unblocked by this one.
- **OPEN QUESTION 2 (producer, scope of AC5):** AC5 currently allows "fixed upstream **or** documented as deferred". Recommendation: raise a core work item for `HelpPanel.ts` / `Overlay.ts` / `SettingsPanel.ts` and document the deferral here, since the submodule cannot be edited from this repo. Confirm that split, or authorise a core-repo session.
- **OPEN QUESTION 3 (producer, scope):** `src/gym/GymCardIndexScene.ts` (`applyScroll`, ~line 373) is a third in-repo `setMask` site of the same class. It is a different scene, so AC3's MainStreetScene boot would not catch it. Should it be folded into this item's ACs (widen AC1/AC2 to "all in-repo viewport masks"), or split into its own follow-up item? Recommendation: fold it in if the fix is a shared helper (one extra call site, one extra test), otherwise split.
- **OPEN QUESTION 4 (engineering, approach):** is a Phaser 4 `Mask` filter actually usable on a `Container` in rc.7? Unverified (see the risky assumption above). Resolution is a short spike — verify a Mask filter clips `streetContainer`, with per-camera viewport clipping as the fallback — before the main implementation slice is scheduled.
